title: Transport of coherent transition associators and units along functor isomorphisms
statement:
Let $I$ be a preordered set and $\mathcal A_i$ categories [def-nagata-category]. Composition is functional, with the rightmost map applied first. For every $i\leq j$ let $B_{ji},C_{ji}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_j$ be functors with specified natural isomorphisms $\chi_{ji}:B_{ji}\cong C_{ji}$. Suppose given natural isomorphisms $d_{kji}:B_{kj}B_{ji}\cong B_{ki}$ and $\lambda_i:B_{ii}\cong1_{\mathcal A_i}$ such that for all $i\leq j\leq k\leq l$ and $K\in\mathcal A_i$,
$$d_{lki,K}\circ B_{lk}(d_{kji,K})=d_{lji,K}\circ d_{lkj,B_{ji}K},$$
$$d_{jii,K}=B_{ji}(\lambda_{i,K}),\qquad d_{jji,K}=\lambda_{j,B_{ji}K}.$$
Use canonical functor reassociations throughout; none of $B_{ii}$, $C_{ii}$ or their unitors is assumed to be an identity. Define
$$z_{kji,K}=\chi_{kj,C_{ji}K}\circ B_{kj}(\chi_{ji,K}),\qquad a_{kji,K}=\chi_{ki,K}\circ d_{kji,K}\circ z_{kji,K}^{-1},\qquad u_{i,K}=\lambda_{i,K}\circ\chi_{ii,K}^{-1}.$$
The maps $a_{kji}$ and $u_i$ are natural isomorphisms and satisfy
$$a_{lki,K}\circ C_{lk}(a_{kji,K})=a_{lji,K}\circ a_{lkj,C_{ji}K},$$
$$a_{jii,K}=C_{ji}(u_{i,K}),\qquad a_{jji,K}=u_{j,C_{ji}K}.$$
In particular they are coherent for arbitrary finite chains, and replacing each $C_{ii}$ by the identity using $u_i$ gives a normalized diagram whose associators with a repeated adjacent index are identities. The comparisons with the ordinary diagram are the specified $\chi$, with $a_{kji}z_{kji}=\chi_{ki}d_{kji}$ and $u_i\chi_{ii}=\lambda_i$.

proof.text: We use the category laws of [def-nagata-category]. A functor preserves identities and composition; thus for an invertible morphism $v$, the map $F(v^{-1})$ is inverse to $F(v)$, by applying $F$ to $vv^{-1}=1$ and $v^{-1}v=1$. For a natural transformation $t:F\to G$, naturality means $G(f)t_X=t_YF(f)$. If all $t_X$ are invertible, multiplication on both sides gives $F(f)t_X^{-1}=t_Y^{-1}G(f)$, so the componentwise inverse is natural. Composites are natural by substituting these equations, and their inverses are the reversed composites of the inverses. These are direct uses of the definitions (Stacks Tags 0014, 0017, 001B, 001I, labels definition-category, definition-isomorphism, definition-functor, definition-transformation-functors in categories.tex).

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: componentwise category and naturality conventions

proof.text: For $f:K\to L$, apply naturality of $\chi_{ji}$ and then of $\chi_{kj}$ to get $$C_{kj}C_{ji}(f)z_{kji,K}=\chi_{kj,C_{ji}L}B_{kj}(C_{ji}(f))B_{kj}(\chi_{ji,K})=z_{kji,L}B_{kj}B_{ji}(f).$$ Its inverse is $$z_{kji,K}^{-1}=B_{kj}(\chi_{ji,K}^{-1})\chi_{kj,C_{ji}K}^{-1}.$$ Multiplying either way gives the identity by step 1. Hence $z_{kji}$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: naturality and invertibility of the two-arrow comparison

proof.text: By step 1, the displayed composites defining $a$ and $u$ are natural. Their componentwise inverses are $z_{kji,K}d_{kji,K}^{-1}\chi_{ki,K}^{-1}$ and $\chi_{ii,K}\lambda_{i,K}^{-1}$, respectively; multiplying proves both inverse equations. Their definitions also give $$a_{kji,K}z_{kji,K}=\chi_{ki,K}d_{kji,K},\qquad u_{i,K}\chi_{ii,K}=\lambda_{i,K}.$$ These are exactly the asserted comparison equations, with the specified $\chi$.

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: construction of the associator and actual unit

proof.text: Fix $i\le j\le k\le l$ and $K\in\mathcal A_i$. Set $$T_K=\chi_{lk,C_{kj}C_{ji}K}\,B_{lk}(\chi_{kj,C_{ji}K})\,B_{lk}B_{kj}(\chi_{ji,K}).$$ It is an isomorphism from $B_{lk}B_{kj}B_{ji}K$ to $C_{lk}C_{kj}C_{ji}K$ by step 1. In particular equality after precomposition by $T_K$ implies equality, by postcomposing on the right with $T_K^{-1}$. Here and below juxtaposition has the functional composition convention of the statement.

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: common invertible comparison for a three-arrow chain

proof.text: Naturality of $\chi_{lk}$ at $a_{kji,K}$ and then step 3 give $$C_{lk}(a_{kji,K})T_K=\chi_{lk,C_{ki}K}B_{lk}(a_{kji,K}z_{kji,K})=z_{lki,K}B_{lk}(d_{kji,K}).$$ Thus the left side of the required associativity equation, precomposed by $T_K$, is $$a_{lki,K}C_{lk}(a_{kji,K})T_K=\chi_{li,K}d_{lki,K}B_{lk}(d_{kji,K}).$$ Each product is well typed; for example $a_{kji,K}$ has source $C_{kj}C_{ji}K$ and target $C_{ki}K$.

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: left path of transported associativity

proof.text: First use step 3 at $C_{ji}K$, and then naturality of $d_{lkj}$ at $\chi_{ji,K}$, to obtain $$a_{lkj,C_{ji}K}T_K=\chi_{lj,C_{ji}K}d_{lkj,C_{ji}K}B_{lk}B_{kj}(\chi_{ji,K})=z_{lji,K}d_{lkj,B_{ji}K}.$$ Consequently the precomposed right path is $$a_{lji,K}a_{lkj,C_{ji}K}T_K=\chi_{li,K}d_{lji,K}d_{lkj,B_{ji}K}.$$ The assumed associativity of $d$ identifies this with step 5. Cancel $T_K$ as in step 4 to prove the required equation for $a$.

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: right path and cancellation against ordinary associativity

proof.text: For the repeated source index, naturality of $\chi_{ji}$ at $u_{i,K}:C_{ii}K\to K$ gives $$C_{ji}(u_{i,K})z_{jii,K}=\chi_{ji,K}B_{ji}(u_{i,K})B_{ji}(\chi_{ii,K})=\chi_{ji,K}B_{ji}(\lambda_{i,K}).$$ By the assumed source-unit law this is $\chi_{ji,K}d_{jii,K}=a_{jii,K}z_{jii,K}$. Cancel $z_{jii,K}$ to get $a_{jii,K}=C_{ji}(u_{i,K})$. No identity assumption on $B_{ii}$ or $C_{ii}$ was used.

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: source-unit equation with the completion unit retained

proof.text: For the repeated target index, substitute the definitions and use naturality of $\lambda_j$ at $\chi_{ji,K}$: $$u_{j,C_{ji}K}z_{jji,K}=\lambda_{j,C_{ji}K}B_{jj}(\chi_{ji,K})=\chi_{ji,K}\lambda_{j,B_{ji}K}=\chi_{ji,K}d_{jji,K}=a_{jji,K}z_{jji,K}.$$ Cancellation proves $a_{jji,K}=u_{j,C_{ji}K}$. This applies also when $i=j$, so the two unit formulas agree on the fully repeated chain.

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: target-unit equation and the fully repeated case

proof.text: For each parenthesized word p, use Word.reduction, recursively whiskering the reductions of both children and then applying a at their endpoint bounds; nil uses the inverse of the actual unit and edge uses identity. Show that every generating Path edge commutes with this reduction. For reassoc, expand both reductions, use naturality of the third reduction at a on the first two bounds, and apply the four-index law. For leftUnit, naturality of the word reduction at the inverse unit and the source-unit law cancel the inverse unit against the unit; rightUnit uses the target-unit law and inverse cancellation. Contract and unit edges cancel immediately. Induct on Path: trans composes the commuting equations, symm cancels the invertible edge, and whisker uses naturality of the second path at the first target reduction and the two induction hypotheses. Thus every path hom followed by the target reduction hom equals the source reduction hom. Cancel the target reduction to obtain FiniteCoherent, including empty chains and repeated indices.

source.place: Proof (3), coefficient convention; agent expansion: explicit finite-chain induction for associators

proof.text: Normalize by an explicit dependent pair: for i=j choose the identity functor together with the actual unit u_i as the comparison rho_ii, and otherwise choose C_ji with its identity comparison. Let N and rho be the projections of this pair. The defining equations give N_ii=identity, rho_ii=u_i, and the off-diagonal identities, including the stated heterogeneous equalities. Apply the proved transport calculation of steps 1–8 to (C,N,rho,a,u), obtaining Coherent N. Apply step 9 to obtain FiniteCoherent N. The normalized unit is rho_ii inverse followed by u_i, hence the identity. Substitute N_ii=identity in each of the two unit laws; functor preservation of identity identifies the repeated-index associators with the canonical left and right functor unitors. All constructions are valid in a preorder without antisymmetry and when the index type is empty.
